summary: The article describes how local education systems are integrating digital literacy and technology into K-12 schooling as of late 2023. It covers a policy mandate from the Education Council, infrastructure investments, teacher training, curriculum changes, student engagement benefits, and efforts to bridge the digital divide.
one_line: Local education authorities are integrating technology and digital literacy into K-12 classrooms through policy, infrastructure, teacher training, curriculum changes and equity efforts.
key_facts: The Education Council, chaired by Dr. Samuel O'Connor, introduced a landmark digital integration policy on September 15, 2023.
The Education Council's policy aims for total technology integration in K-12 education by 2026.
The policy includes educator training, equipping classrooms with technological tools, and a curriculum responsive to technological advancements.
The Morganville School District launched a pilot project led by Superintendent Lisa Reynolds to integrate smartboards, student tablets, and a robust wireless network.
The Lincoln High Tech Learning Center opened on October 10, 2023.
The Henderson County School System started the 'Tech for Teachers' program on November 2, 2023, headed by tech coach Emily Torres.
School boards have updated learning objectives to include coding, digital content creation, online safety, and critical evaluation of digital media.
The Franklin Elementary School District has led in implementing digital storytelling projects that improve technical skills and learning in language arts and social studies.
Josephine Hart, a 4th grader with dyslexia, has improved her reading skills using adaptive learning software that tailors to her pace and style.
A Johnston Institute for Educational Research study published December 12, 2023 found 87% of students feel more engaged in classrooms where technology is used.
Anne-Marie Davidson leads local education committees in Little Rock, Arkansas, working to ensure equitable access to technology.
Equity initiatives include Wi-Fi hotspots and low-cost or no-cost devices for low-income families to bridge the digital divide.
